2.4.evaluator_rationale: While the policy mentions strengthening institutional capacity on gender, it does not explicitly establish or require gender mainstreaming as an institutional mechanism for implementing women’s protection or VAW policies/programs in the provided sentences.

evidence_candidates.text:
CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Bandung Regency.
2. Regent is the Regent of Bandung.
3. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
4. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and the Regional House of Representatives in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the Region.
5. Women are human beings of female gender starting from infants, adolescents, adults up to the elderly, who have been recognized by law.
6. Prevention is activities carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against Women.
7. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily.
8. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Regional Government, community, and/or other parties who know or hear that violence against Women will or has occurred.
9. Victim is a Woman who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence and life vulnerability.
10. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social and psychological to the victim.
11. Victim of Violence is an individual or group of people who experience suffering whether physical, mental or emotional, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights violations or criminal acts as well as acts of Violence committed either by state apparatus, Regional Government apparatus, or individuals.
12. Violence Against Women is any action that results in or may result in misery or suffering to Women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
13. Family is a person who has a blood relationship in a straight line upward or downward and collateral line up to the third degree, or who has a marital relationship, or a person who is a dependent of a Woman.
14. Parents are biological father and/or mother, step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
15. Discrimination Against Women is any distinction, exclusion, or restriction made on the basis of sex which has the effect or purpose of impairing or nullifying the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural, civil, or any other field by Women, irrespective of their marital status on the basis of equality between men and Women.
16. Gender is a concept that refers to the differentiation of roles and responsibilities of men and Women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural circumstances of society.
17. Health Rehabilitation is an effort to restore the condition of Victims including physical, psychological, and sexual health so that Victims can carry out their roles again properly and naturally both in the family and in society.
18. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person who experiences social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly.
19. Repatriation is an effort to return Victims of Violence to their region of origin.
20. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite Victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide Protection and fulfillment of needs for Victims.
21. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment hereinafter referred to as P2TP2A is an integrated service unit established by the Regional Government to carry out the functions and main tasks of integrated services for Women and children Victims of Violence, including complaint services, Health Rehabilitation, Social Rehabilitation, Repatriation, Social Reintegration, and legal assistance.

Article 23
(1) The Regent shall conduct supervision over the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of Women.
(2) To ensure synergy, continuity, and effectiveness in an integrated manner in the implementation of supervision as referred to in paragraph (1), the Regent shall conduct monitoring through the Regional Apparatus handling the field of Women.
(3) Monitoring as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be conducted from planning to implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of Women for the current year.
(4) The results of monitoring as referred to in paragraph (3) shall be reported to the Regent periodically.

Article 26
Further provisions regarding the supervision, evaluation, and guidance of policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of Women as referred to in Article 21 through Article 23 shall be regulated by a Regent Regulation.

Article 25
The Regent provides guidance on the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of Women to the relevant Regional Apparatus and sub-districts.

Article 24
(1) The Regional Government conducts an evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of Women at the end of each fiscal year.
(2) The results of the evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) are used as input material for the formulation of policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of Women for the following year.
(3) The evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

CHAPTER VII
COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION
Article 21
(1) Community participation in the Protection of Women may take the form of:
a. provision of counseling regarding the rights of Women;
b. provision of skills training to support the Family economy;
c. establishment of community social institutions to assist Victims of Violence; and
d. reporting to the competent authorities if Violence Against Women occurs in their environment.
(2) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may be carried out by individuals, community social institutions, non-governmental organizations, educational institutions, religious institutions, the private sector, and mass media.

Article 16
(1) The provision of services for the Protection of Women as referred to in Article 14 consists of identification of Victims, legal aid, medical rehabilitation, psychosocial rehabilitation, Social Reintegration, repatriation assistance.
(2) The provision of services for the Protection of Women as referred to in paragraph (1) is provided for Women Victims of Violence including victims of trafficking in persons, Women in disaster-prone areas, Women workers, elderly Women, Women with disabilities, and Women Victims of sexual exploitation.

Article 23
Paragraph (1) Sufficiently clear.
Paragraph (2) What is meant by Monitoring is to determine the developments and obstacles in the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of women.
Paragraph (3) Sufficiently clear.
Paragraph (4) Sufficiently clear.

Part One
Prevention of Violence Against Women

CHAPTER IX
FINANCING
Article 27
Financing for the implementation of Women's Protection is sourced from:
a. regional revenue and expenditure budget; and b. other legitimate and non-binding sources of funds

CHAPTER V
PREVENTION, PROTECTION SERVICES, AND RECOVERY OF VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE AGAINST WOMEN

Article 18
Further provisions regarding the procedures for prevention, protection services, and Recovery of Victims of Violence Against Women as referred to in Article 13 up to Article 17 shall be regulated by a Regent's Regulation.

2.4.rationale: The original Indonesian text does institutionalise gender mainstreaming elements through explicit integration into planning/budgeting and institutional strengthening, which the retrieved English candidates already contain. In Pasal 8(1)-(4), the Regent must “mengintegrasikan kebijakan, program, dan kegiatan Perlindungan Perempuan ke dalam perencanaan pembangunan Daerah” and this integration must be put into formal planning and budget documents (RPJPD, RPJMD, Renstra perangkat daerah, RKPD, RKA). This is a concrete institutional mechanism akin to mainstreaming (integrating women’s protection/gender-related policy into core government planning and budgeting systems). Additionally, Pasal 10(1)(c) mandates “penguatan kapasitas kelembagaan Gender” (strengthening gender institutional capacity). These provisions were present in the retrieved passages ([2.4-14] Article 8 and [2.4-16] Article 10), so a judge limited to those candidates could reasonably answer Yes. The judge’s rationale was overly narrow/strict by requiring the exact phrase “gender mainstreaming” rather than recognizing that mandated integration into development planning/budgeting and gender institutional capacity strengthening constitutes mainstreaming institutionalisation in this regulation.
